title: Astrid and the Garden
premise: Jude Nakamura has spent a decade hiding her forbidden gift of swordspeech in the smuggler warrens of Thornfell, until the old gods—long silent since the kingdom's collapse—begin answering the desperate prayers of common folk. Hunted by the Regency's inquisitors and bound by an oath she swore to a dead queen, Jude must guide a ragged found family of believers to the Garden, a mythical door said to lead out of a country that officially no longer exists. Along the way she must choose between loyalty to her oath and the truth that the gods are answering prayers not with mercy but with judgment. In the end, Jude breaks her oath publicly at the Garden's threshold, speaking truth to the assembled faithful—and the door opens not for escape but for accountability, binding the survivors to rebuild rather than flee.
about_author: Casper Voss is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent years mapping mountain passes across three continents before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders, oaths, and the people who live in the gaps between them.

chapters.title: The Salt Road Prayer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. While guiding contraband through Thornfell's high passes, Jude witnesses a dying miner's prayer answered by a god long thought dead—the mountain itself rises to bury his corrupt overseers. Terrified, she recognizes the answering voice as one her oath once served. The emotional beat is dread: invisibility, her life's strategy, is now impossible.

chapters.title: A Congregation of Strays
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with interludes from Sefa, a runaway acolyte. Word spreads; pilgrims and fugitives gather around Jude believing her a prophet. She reluctantly shelters them—an orphaned thief, a disgraced inquisitor's daughter, old Sefa—in her hidden waystation. When Regency riders burn a neighboring village seeking 'the swordspeaker,' loyalty to her strays begins outweighing her instinct to run.

chapters.title: What the Gods Want Back
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Jude and the inquisitor Halvard Vane. The gods' answers turn cruel—a village healed of plague, then demanded sacrifice. Jude learns her oath was never protection but a leash: the dead queen bound the gods' hunger through swordspeakers like her. Climax builds as Vane corners the group at the Garden's threshold, and Jude realizes escape was always the trap.

chapters.title: The Door That Opens Both Ways
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the Garden, the door demands an oath renewed; instead Jude speaks her broken truth aloud—that the gods were caged, not worshipped, and the country died hiding it. The door opens onto the ruined capital, not freedom, forcing the faithful to see what they fled. Vane lowers his blade; the strays choose to stay and rebuild. Resolution: found family over escape, truth over loyalty.
